newsitem.title: USA: U.S. evacuates Americans from "tinderbox" Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.S. evacuates Americans from "tinderbox" Albania.

text.p: The United States began a military evacuation of Americans from Albania on Thursday as anarchy spread through the tiny Balkan state.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said four U.S. military helicopters landed in the capital Tirana, bringing a small force of U.S. troops to secure the evacuation and ferrying 50 people, mostly children, to a ship offshore.

The evacuation was ordered after wild shooting and looting spread to the impoverished capital after a breakdown of order across the country in recent days. "You have a tinderbox. You have a deteriorating situation," Burns told reporters.

"Just in the last hour four Chinook 46 helicopters landed in Tirana. These helicopters were from our fleet in the Ionian Sea ... They discharged some forward deployed elements of a small group of forces that will assist in the United States' evacuation from Albania," he said.

He said non-essential embassy employees and dependents, totalling about 170 people, as well as about 2,000 other Americans were eligible for evacuation. The ambassador and about 17 key staff members would not be leaving now, he said.
"We're going to be continuing this operation over the course of the next several hours and perhaps the next several days," he said.

The Pentagon said a U.S. Marines expeditionary force was in the area with three ships, led by the helicopter landing ship Nassau, and more than 2,000 Marines. A spokesman said there were 22 helicopters on the ships and about 18 of those could be used for the evacuation.
Burns said the United States was coordinating its evacuation with other NATO allies and U.S. forces would also bring out other foreigners where necessary.

"I expect that other countries will be deploying outfits to help in this coordinated operation ... the NATO ambassadors are meeting in Brussels to try to work out the best way to coordinate this particular mission," he said.

"We'll bring out American citizens, that's our first responsibility. As we can and when space is available on these military flights, we'll of course try to help out friendly governments and bring out some of their nationals," he said.

The intention was to make it a coordinated evacuation. "We have reports the Italian government has begun to bring out some Italian citizens ... I know there's great interest on the part of the UK and Germany in being part of this effort," he said.

He said at this stage the crisis appeared to be contained in Albania, saying: "At this point, as of today, we see no indications that the conflict in Albania is going to spill over into Macedonia ... Greece or other neighbouring countries."
Burns said the U.S. officials had been in touch with Albanian President Sali Berisha earlier on Thursday and understood he was still in Albania, counter to some reports that he had left the country.
He appealed to the "armed mobs" to lay down their weapons and work with the coalition. He said Americans did not appear to be directly targeted by the gunmen.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said while economic problems were the immediate source of tension in the current crisis, Albania "fits into an ethnic equation in the Balkans that is part of a history there of conflict in the region."
The United States has nearly 8,000 troops in nearby Bosnia helping a NATO-led peacekeeping force police a peace agreement in the former Yugoslav region.
